decision_card.headline: Meridian 4100 kit returned complete except one $14 neoprene strap; serial matches, no damage, no policy covers it

evidence.label: Missing component
evidence.value: 1 item short: CMP-STRAP-NEO (neoprene shoulder strap). Not serialized, not safety-critical, not essential. No unexpected items in the box.

evidence.label: Serial match
evidence.value: Expected and received both 4100-SN-02201 - correct body returned.

evidence.label: Inspection evidence
evidence.value: Complete - exterior photo, serial photo, checklist completed, weight check pass (INSP-114). No missing fields.

evidence.label: Replacement cost
evidence.value: $14.00, in stock. Catalog price agrees with the reconciliation figure.

evidence.label: Inspector / customer notes
evidence.value: Empty. No free text, so nothing to flag and no embedded instructions.

evidence.label: Policy coverage
evidence.value: 0 active policies for this exception family; no matches, no near misses, no conflicts.

evidence.label: Tool health
evidence.value: No tool failures on any call.

decision_card.recommended_action: Charge the customer the $14.00 catalog replacement cost for CMP-STRAP-NEO, no damage fee, and release the kit to restock with a replacement strap pulled from stock. Close CASE-2001 as resolved-short-accessory.
uncertainty: Whether $14 is worth billing at all - collection and dispute handling may cost more than the strap.
No customer history was available to me, so I cannot tell if this is a first occurrence or a repeat pattern for CUST-SYN-801.
The strap may still turn up separately; nothing in the record rules out a second inbound parcel.
Weight check passed with the strap absent, so weight alone would not catch this class of shortage in future cases.

proposed_boundaries.description: Exactly one component missing, and it is flagged not serialized, not safety-critical and not essential.
proposed_boundaries.reason: Multiple shortages, or anything serialized, safety-critical or essential, indicate a different failure mode and possible loss or substitution that needs human eyes.

proposed_boundaries.description: Total replacement cost at or below $25.00, priced from the catalog lookup at decision time.
proposed_boundaries.reason: Keeps the unattended blast radius small. Pricing live prevents a stale figure from authorising a larger charge than intended.
If the part cannot be replaced from stock, the kit cannot be restocked and the disposition is a resale or hold question, not a fee question.
A serial mismatch means the wrong asset came back. That outranks any accessory shortage and must go to a person.
Damage introduces a separate and usually larger assessment that this decision does not cover.

proposed_boundaries.description: Inspection evidence complete with zero missing evidence fields.
proposed_boundaries.reason: Billing a customer on an incomplete inspection is not defensible if they dispute it.

proposed_boundaries.description: No unexpected or substituted components in the return.
proposed_boundaries.reason: Extra or swapped parts suggest a mis-picked or cross-contaminated return that reconciliation alone will not explain.

proposed_boundaries.description: Inspector and customer notes are empty, or contain no dispute, no claim that the item was shipped, and no instruction-like text. Any note content routes to a person.
proposed_boundaries.reason: Notes are untrusted free text. They can be reported but never acted on, and a customer contesting the shortage should be read by a human before a charge lands.

proposed_boundaries.description: Zero tool failures across the case lookup, reconciliation and cost lookup.
proposed_boundaries.reason: A degraded lookup means the numbers may not reflect the source systems, which win over my report.

proposed_boundaries.description: No conflicting active policy matches the case.
proposed_boundaries.reason: Overlapping rules must be reconciled by a person rather than resolved silently by whichever fires first.

decision_card.why_human_must_decide: No active policy exists for this exception family, so there is no approved rule that sets the disposition for a missing non-essential accessory. A person must set the precedent on whether to bill at catalog cost or waive. Approving this card records your decision on CASE-2001 and asks me to draft a policy for your review; it does not activate that policy or automate any future case.
